episode.title: Restore resumed sessions through the canonical persisted provider route
episode.before: At parent commit 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the Desktop/TUI resume reader independently extracted only top-level provider, base_url, and api_mode values from model_config, then fell back to billing_provider. It did not inspect model_config.gateway_runtime, even though the messaging gateway persisted the most recently executed route there on each turn. Consequently, after a session changed providers, Desktop resume could combine the stored model with a stale first-call billing provider or stale top-level endpoint and wire settings.
episode.after: At commit 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, Desktop/TUI resume delegates persisted-route selection to the same SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime reader used by CLI resume. That reader prioritizes a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime route, otherwise retains top-level provider/base_url/api_mode data and fills only a missing provider from a routable billing_provider. Existing downstream endpoint-safety, provider-healing, reasoning, and service-tier handling remains in the Desktop resume path.
episode.diff: The change removes the duplicate route-selection logic and local bare-billing-provider import from tui_gateway/server.py, calls SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row), and converts its provider/base_url/api_mode result into resume overrides. It adjusts the canonical reader so billing_provider supplements, rather than loses to, partial top-level route metadata. Two regression tests establish that nested gateway_runtime wins over both a stale first-call billing_provider and stale top-level route keys, while existing tests cover nested/top-level precedence, invalid metadata, bare billing buckets, and routable billing-provider fallback.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480 identifies the defect as Desktop/TUI resume ignoring the nested gateway_runtime persisted per turn and reports the two added tests as red on the base and green on the commit.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and commit_show_stat

evidence_units.claim: The messaging turn path snapshots provider, base_url, api_mode, and fallback state from the active agent and writes that snapshot into model_config.gateway_runtime together with the current model.

The canonical persisted-route reader parses model_config, prefers a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime dictionary, then reads top-level provider/base_url/api_mode, and ignores unroutable bare billing buckets.

The canonical reader changed from returning any nonempty top-level route before considering billing_provider to supplementing a partial top-level route with a routable billing_provider via setdefault, preserving top-level endpoint and wire metadata when provider is absent.

The Desktop/TUI resume reader removed its hand-written top-level and billing-provider selection and now obtains provider, base_url, and api_mode from SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row); service_tier and the later endpoint-safety and provider-healing logic remain local.

Deferred, cold, and eager Desktop/TUI session-resume paths all call _stored_session_runtime_overrides and pass the resulting persisted runtime identity into the resumed session record or agent construction.

CLI resume also reads the persisted route through SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime, demonstrating that the changed Desktop path now shares the established route-selection boundary with another resume consumer.

A new regression test constructs a row whose billing_provider is stale but whose nested gateway_runtime contains the last provider and API mode, and requires both Desktop and CLI readers to restore the nested route.

A second new regression test constructs stale top-level route keys plus a newer nested gateway_runtime and requires Desktop resume to choose the nested provider and API mode without retaining the stale endpoint.

Existing canonical-reader tests cover nested-over-top-level precedence, top-level fallback, malformed metadata, routable billing-provider fallback, rejection of bare billing buckets, and explicit-provider precedence over billing data.

Existing Desktop/TUI tests require bare billing buckets to remain unset, routable billing providers such as anthropic and openrouter to be restored, and an explicit routable provider to win over a bare billing bucket.
The pinned diff passes Git whitespace/error validation.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-partial-persisted-route-fallback
candidate_atomics.title: Complete a partial persisted route without discarding its endpoint metadata
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize layered session metadata so the canonical reader preserves explicit top-level endpoint and wire fields while filling only a missing provider from a routable historical fallback.

semantic_action.intent: Produce one usable persisted runtime route from layered session metadata without replacing newer or more specific route fields with a stale or non-routable fallback identity.
semantic_action.pre_state: A session row may contain a provider-bearing nested runtime snapshot, partial top-level route fields, a routable billing provider, a bare non-routable billing bucket, malformed configuration, or combinations of these states.
semantic_action.post_state: A provider-bearing nested runtime route wins; otherwise top-level route fields are retained and a routable billing provider fills only an absent provider; bare billing buckets and malformed metadata do not create a provider override.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise nested precedence, partial top-level fallback, malformed metadata, routable billing fallback, bare-bucket rejection, and explicit-provider precedence through the canonical reader tests.

candidate_atomics.name: delegate-resume-route-selection-to-canonical-reader
candidate_atomics.title: Use the canonical persisted route when rebuilding a resumed client session
candidate_atomics.description: Adapt a resume interface that had its own incomplete metadata reader to consume the canonical route resolver, while leaving its interface-specific override construction and safety repairs intact.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure every resume interface restores the provider, endpoint, and protocol belonging to the session's latest persisted runtime route.
semantic_action.pre_state: The resume adapter independently reads only top-level route fields and billing metadata, while another execution path persists the latest route in a nested runtime snapshot and another resume consumer already uses the canonical resolver.
semantic_action.post_state: The resume adapter obtains provider, endpoint, and API mode through the canonical resolver, then applies its existing endpoint-ownership checks, provider healing, and override construction.
semantic_action.validation: Assert that resume selects nested runtime data over a stale first-call billing provider and over stale top-level route keys, and compare the restored route with the existing CLI resume consumer.

candidate_workflows.name: align-resume-interface-with-persisted-runtime-route
candidate_workflows.title: Align a resume interface with the authoritative persisted runtime route
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve cross-interface resume failures by identifying the metadata actually updated by the producer, defining a single precedence contract for legacy and current representations, and routing the inconsistent consumer through that contract while preserving its local safety behavior.

workflow_graph.goal: A session resumed through any supported interface uses the provider, endpoint, and protocol associated with its latest persisted runtime execution rather than combining its model with stale route metadata.
when_to_use: A producer and one resume consumer use a nested or versioned runtime snapshot while another consumer reconstructs the same route from older top-level or accounting fields.
A resumed model is sent to the wrong provider endpoint or protocol after the session changes providers.
Multiple consumers interpret the same persisted route with different precedence rules.
anti_goals: Do not change provider selection for new sessions that have no usable persisted route.
Do not treat accounting buckets as authoritative route identities when they are documented as frozen or non-routable.
Do not remove interface-specific endpoint-ownership checks, stale-provider healing, reasoning settings, service-tier handling, or profile-following behavior.
Do not persist or restore raw API credentials as part of route reconciliation.
not_applicable_when: There is no durable runtime-route representation or no evidence identifying which representation is freshest.
The failure occurs during initial provider discovery rather than restoration of an existing session.
The differing consumers intentionally implement distinct routing semantics rather than alternate interfaces to the same resumed session.
inputs: Persisted session-row shapes from every writer
All resume consumers of the stored route
Documented route-field precedence and non-routable fallback values
Regression tests representing stale and current metadata combinations
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least one resume interface can read a stale provider, endpoint, or API mode because its local metadata interpretation differs from the writer and from another resume consumer.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All examined resume interfaces consume the same canonical route precedence, the latest nested route wins over stale representations, partial legacy metadata remains compatible, and unsafe fallback identities remain filtered.

steps.condition: The persisted row has multiple current or legacy route representations whose precedence and fallback composition must be made explicit.
steps.validation: Canonical-reader tests prove nested precedence, legacy top-level support, routable fallback completion, bare-bucket rejection, and malformed-input tolerance.

steps.condition: A resume consumer independently decodes route metadata instead of using the established canonical resolver.
steps.validation: Cross-interface regression tests prove the adapted consumer and the existing canonical consumer select the nested current route over stale billing and top-level values.

validation_ladder: Inspect the writer to confirm which persisted representation is refreshed on each executed turn.
Unit-test the canonical resolver across nested, top-level, partial, malformed, routable-fallback, and non-routable-fallback inputs.
Run consumer-level regression tests with a stale first-call billing provider and a newer nested route.
Run consumer-level regression tests with stale top-level endpoint/protocol keys and a newer nested route.
Run existing resume compatibility tests for endpoint ownership, provider healing, legacy rows, profile-following exclusions, reasoning configuration, and service tier.
Run repository diff validation and the focused test module in the supported project environment.
stop_conditions: Stop if the producer's authoritative or freshest representation cannot be established from code or tests.
Stop if the proposed canonical precedence would discard a supported legacy route representation without a migration or compatibility oracle.
Stop if the consumer has intentionally different routing semantics and therefore should not share the resolver.
Do not claim runtime validation complete unless the focused tests execute successfully in a dependency-complete environment.
